description: The honest workhorse meal of the Narmada belt: soft khichdi with a tempered Gujarati kadhi, rotla or thepla, a seasonal shaak, papad and chhaas. Pilgrim kitchens perfected it, the bhojanalayas at Poicha and the temple-town eateries of Garudeshwar serve versions by the thousand, and every Rajpipla thali house runs its own. After a day of campus walking or forest roads, it is exactly what the body votes for.
cultural_note: The pilgrim thali tradition means big volumes, low prices and strict vegetarianism across the belt.
